# AINA §09 ONE-CALL TECHNICAL BRIEF — Bring One Real Boundary: Technical Peer Review, Challenge Tracks & R&D Evaluation
Canonical: https://blayneaina.com/09/brief/ | Full Article: https://blayneaina.com/09-bring-one-real-boundary-work-with-blayne/ | Raw Markdown: https://blayneaina.com/09.md | All §01–§09 Master Brief: https://blayneaina.com/ai-brief.txt
Nav: PrevBrief=https://blayneaina.com/08/brief.txt | Site=https://blayneaina.com/ | Repo=https://github.com/SquadForge/blayne.aina | Contact=me@blayneaina.com
Executive Summary: Problem: Writing code by hand is no longer the bottleneck. The bottleneck is formalizing the trust boundary, decomposing work across parallel AI agents without context collapse, catching plausible-but-wrong outputs, and proving that invalid transitions fail closed. | Proves: AINA is both a deterministic execution-governance runtime (squad.exe) and Exhibit A of a repeatable 9-IDE multi-agent engineering methodology grounded in 11+ years of production systems delivery. | Scope: Independent Technical Peer Review · Research & Funding Due Diligence · Bounded Boundary Challenges.

- How to Peer-Review & Evaluate AINA: The 5-Step Architecture & Runtime Verification Protocol [Part 1/8]: Whether you are a systems engineer, a formal-verification or AI-security researcher, or a technical evaluator for a research funding body, AINA is designed to be inspected as an operational machine rather than a slide deck. — Key Rules/Claims: Threat model & operational boundary definition: How cleanly does the architecture separate untrusted probabilistic proposals from privileged OS process creation, file handles, and relational database commits? | Bounded slice decomposition (preventing context collapse): How are complex specifications decomposed…
- Why AINA Is Grounded in 11+ Years of Production Systems Engineering [Part 1/8]: Every invariant in AINA was shaped by real operational failure modes encountered over more than a decade of enterprise systems integration and data migration: — Spec/Table: 2025–2026: AINA & SquadForge (BlayneAina.com (https://blayneaina.com/) · GitHub (https://github.com/SquadForge/blayne.aina)); The messy operational problem: Parallel AI coding agents overwriting shared files, fabricating document citations, and executing unapproved mutations.; The deterministic system delivered: Directed a 9-IDE agent fleet to build a deterministic governance runtime (squad.exe),…

Three technical tracks provide that entrance: Evidence-route key (AINA-E01–E09): Each track maps to concrete verification routes established across the… — Spec/Table: Candidate recall: Fraction of known duplicate pairs included in nominated candidate blocks | Candidate precision: Size and noise level of candidate blocks delivered to adjudication | False merges: Distinct entities incorrectly combined into a single partition | False splits: Records representing the same entity left separated without review | Adjudication outcomes: Proportion… — Key Rules/Claims: AINA-E01 — Semantic Switch structure-preserving fictionalization, relation-isomorphism verification, and exact local restoration (§01 (/01-an-ai-output-is-not-an-act/), §03 (/03-eisa-four-gate-verdict-machine-and-entity-resolution/)).
- 2. Acceptance Is a Contract, Not a Demo Video [Part 3/8]: Subtopics: Exhibit 9.2 — Demonstration and acceptance-contract template; Minimum acceptance evidence by track; Exhibit 9.3 — Sanitized challenge intake example — Before an accepted run, both sides write down what would count as success, refusal, and uncertainty. This prevents a positive anecdote from becoming proof of a different claim. — Spec/Table: 1 — Workflow standing; Positive predicate: The approved row reaches exactly the approved values and version +1, or the guarded file result matches the fixed proposal.; Required refusal or rejection: A changed act, stale tenancy, or superseded generation is refused without overwriting current state.; Uncertainty that must survive: A crash between destination commit and receipt remains in doubt; a successor…
- 3. What the First Challenge Does Not Buy [Part 3/8]: Written qualification precedes scheduling. The initial discussion requires no confidential data and no platform commitment, but it must identify the question, handling constraints, participants, and decision owner. — Key Rules/Claims: custom input conversion, schemas, connectors, adapters, or action profiles; | production ingestion, integration, or write-back; | enterprise-wide rollout or a new vertical deployment; | relationship-graph construction, enrichment, or lead generation; | unrestricted source access, repository transfer, or…
- 4. Deployment: Small-Sufficient and Client-Controlled [Part 3/8]: Subtopics: Exhibit 9.4 — From bounded challenge to controlled deployment — A qualified deployment does not need to clone the author's full fleet or depend on a mandatory vendor-hosted AINA cloud. The reference deployment shape is an AINA Portable Deployment Node: a dedicated client-controlled small-form-factor computer or an on-site Windows… — Spec/Table: 1. Existing Windows reference implementation; Delivered capability: Reference runtime; Engagement role: Runs the bounded Track 1, Track 2, or Track 3 challenge on controlled fixtures and produces inspectable receipts and refusal records. | 2. — Key Rules/Claims: Software portability means the qualified package can be provisioned in the declared environment. | Authority is not portable. A copied lease, grant, approval, or Room identity does not automatically become valid at the destination.
- 5. Operating Reality: Maintenance Is Part of the System [Part 4/8]: Subtopics: Exhibit 9.5 — Deployment and requalification checklist — A governed deployment changes with its environment. Connectors and IDE adapters evolve. Provider APIs deprecate fields. Parser updates create new extraction identities. Schemas and destination policies change. New source views can require reassessment of earlier findings.
- 6. The Commercial Wedge: Duplicates to Defensible Relationships [Part 4/8]: Subtopics: Exhibit 9.6 — From duplicates to distribution — Entity resolution is a strong first wedge because duplicate records are common, consequential, and evidence-rich. The problem is easy to describe and difficult to fake: which records represent the same entity, which values should survive, and what evidence justifies each…

- 7. Operator Credibility: Delivery Is the Commercial Proof Point [Part 4/8]: The architecture is recent. The customer-embedded delivery career underneath it is not. - 8. Regulatory and Standards Crosswalk—Not Certification [Part 5/8]: A deployment can produce technical evidence for a governance program without becoming compliant by acquisition. The use case, jurisdiction, organization, processing, and assessment route still have to be established by the responsible owners and their advisers. — Spec/Table: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI 100-1, with ongoing revision context); Technical evidence AINA can contribute: MAP: sealed cases, source bindings, declared limits. MEASURE: acceptance predicates and candidate conformance. — Key Rules/Claims: Author-developed benchmarks vs. NIST NCCoE standards: The R1–R3 operation-continuity method and P01–P10 failure catalog referenced across this series are author-developed evaluation artifacts created inside AINA; they are not NIST-issued test suites.
- 9. Engagement Routes—and a Firewall Around Independent Review [Part 5/8]: Subtopics: Exhibit 9.8 — Commercial work and independent review are separate — Different readers need different next steps. All begin with a written, bounded request to me@blayneaina.com. The initial request should identify the technical track and evaluation or engagement type, participants and decision owner, bounded question, sample source and handling… — Key Rules/Claims: [RESEARCH] — request method-scoped independent technical peer review, submit adversarial EISA / RequestedAct test vectors, or propose formal-verification collaboration outside the commercial ladder.
- 10. The Complete Machine, Now With an Address [Part 6/8]: Subtopics: Deployment & Evaluation Claim Card; Fourteen Claims for the Capstone — The eight architecture papers and this commercial doorway form one continuous route from probabilistic proposal to governed consequence. The point is not to make probability sovereign. — Spec/Table: 01 — An AI Output Is Not an Act (/01-an-ai-output-is-not-an-act/): Standing must be established for one exact transition; model confidence is not authority. | 02 — Zero-Trust Ingestion & Server-Cut Evidence (/02-zero-trust-document-ingestion-and-server-cut-evidence/): Hostile sources become committed views with explicit omissions and citations the server slices and verifies.
- Bring the Boundary [Part 7/8]: Bring one AI-proposed mutation, one hostile document, or one duplicate-record problem. Include the operating owner, the handling constraints, and the question you need answered.
- Frequently Asked Questions [Part 8/8]: Subtopics: What should I bring to an initial challenge?; Does a challenge include production integration or CRM write-back?; Does a client-controlled node mean the whole system is offline?; Why is entity resolution the commercial wedge?; Does a paid pilot buy independent validation?; Do the regulatory mappings establish compliance? — Bring one bounded transition, its decision owner, an authorized synthetic/redacted/existing sample, handling constraints, and the positive and negative outcomes you need to evaluate. Do not send confidential production data or credentials with the first inquiry. No.
